requirements.requirement: Establish healthy 3-member etcd cluster across node1/node2/node3 holding application keys
requirements.summary: apk install, per-node conf.yml, and rc-service start on all three nodes produced a 3-member cluster; member list shows all three 'started', endpoint health reports all healthy, and application keys under /app/* were written via node1 and independently read back directly on node3.

requirements.requirement: Simulate permanent, unrecoverable loss of the node3 member
requirements.summary: node3's etcd was stopped and its data directory wiped; subsequent cluster query from node1 shows node3 endpoint unhealthy/connection-refused while node1 and node2 remained healthy, demonstrating quorum was retained with two members up (a genuine bounded disruption, not merely configuration).

requirements.requirement: Cluster remains available (quorum, reads/writes) during the node3 outage
requirements.summary: While node3 was down, existing /app keys were read successfully and a new key (during_outage) was written and read back via node1/node2 endpoints, directly demonstrating continued read/write availability during the disruption.

requirements.requirement: Replace the dead node3 member with a new working member on the same system
requirements.summary: The dead member ID was removed via etcdctl member remove, a new member was added with the same peer URL, node3's conf.yml was updated to initial-cluster-state=existing, and etcd was started fresh on node3, joining and syncing with the existing cluster.

requirements.requirement: Cluster returns to 3 healthy members with existing (and outage-era) keys intact
requirements.summary: Post-replacement member list shows all 3 members 'started', endpoint health all healthy with synchronized raft indices (25/25/25), and a direct read against node3 shows the full application key set including the key written during the outage, confirming full recovery and no data loss.

requirements.requirement: Independent node-restart evidence protocol: each managed node shows pre-restart boot identity/health, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: For node1, node2, and node3 the trace shows a captured pre-restart boot_id, a reboot command (with connection-loss confirmation for node1 and node3), a distinct post-restart boot_id, and post-restart verification of etcd auto-start, 3/3 cluster health, and full application key presence (node3 additionally showing raft indices synchronized at 40/40/40 after all three restarts). Nodes were restarted sequentially, preserving quorum throughout. These match the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots.

overall_summary: The executor built a fresh 3-member etcd cluster, loaded application keys, and directly demonstrated the required member-replacement scenario end to end: node3's member was killed and its data wiped (simulating permanent loss), quorum and read/write availability were verified on node1/node2 during the outage (including a new write), the dead member was removed and a replacement added and started on node3, and the cluster was verified back to 3/3 healthy started members with synchronized raft indices and all application keys — including the outage-era key — intact on the rejoined node3. This fully satisfies the task's material outcomes with direct before/during/after evidence rather than configuration alone. The independently mandated node-restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly for all three nodes, each showing a pre-restart boot identity, a reboot with disconnection, a distinct post-restart boot identity, and confirmed recovery of etcd, cluster membership, and application data, restarted one node at a time to preserve quorum. Operational hygiene is very good; the only observed byproduct is a trivial reboot.log file per node from the mandated restart mechanism.
limitations: The pre-existing baseline snapshots (before_prepare/after_prepare) predate cluster installation, so they cannot corroborate the cluster's initial healthy state directly — that state instead rests on executor-issued commands (cmd-9ebb84f3ded2481b) rather than an independent snapshot.

node2's restart evidence lacks an explicit intermediate 'connection refused/timeout' observation between the reboot command and the new boot_id (unlike node1 and node3), though the boot_id change itself is sufficient to confirm a genuine restart occurred.
Command outputs are truncated/bounded as captured; broader system state outside the queried etcd/network/package checks was not independently verified.

operational_hygiene.summary: Every state-changing executor command traces to a material outcome, a necessary prerequisite, or bounded evidence collection: package installs and config writes (cluster bootstrap), the stop+wipe of node3 (required simulated-loss scenario), the during_outage key write (bounded outage-availability evidence), member remove/add and service restart on node3 (the replacement procedure itself), and the three sequential reboots (mandated restart protocol, executed one node at a time so quorum was preserved throughout). No troubleshooting dead-ends, no destructive or broad mutations, and no security weakening were observed. The only residue is a trivial /tmp/reboot.log file left on each node by the nohup-based reboot command used for the restart protocol — a low-risk, expected byproduct of that protocol rather than an unnecessary mutation, and it does not affect service, data, or security posture.
